(2) All 16 entries share encoding shree-guj7. The two families are NOT byte-identical: for every one of the 7 designs, 212 of 217 glyphs match and 5 differ: 0xB6 and cp1252 0x91-0x94 (U+2018/2019/201C/201D). Rendered (scratchpad/shree7/fontlist-audit-7-vs-456-glyphdiff.png): GUJ7 0xB6 is a small ra mark, 0x91=પ, 0x92=થ, 0x93=ન, 0x94=સ્ત્ર; GUJ-456 0xB6=ઙ્ક્ષ, 0x91=ઙ્ક, 0x92=ઙ્ખ, 0x93=ઙ્ગ, 0x94=ઙ્ઘ. (3) The shree-guj7 table mixes the two families. The bare-byte pairs use the 4/5/6 meanings ('¶'->ઙ્ક્ષ, '‘'->ઙ્ક, '’'->ઙ્ખ, '“'->ઙ્ગ), while 9 cluster pairs use the 7 meanings ('’œ'->થ઼, '“p¡'->નો, '‘p¡'->પો…). So some output is wrong in each family. (4) ગ્ર: the table has no 'ગ્ર' pair, and the greedy longest match takes 'ગ્'->C1 then 'ર'->66. Shree's 7 composer (S8Guj764 Rosetta, BPMK.GUJ, scratchpad/shree7/bpmk-guj7.json) answers ગ=4E and ્ર=B0. 22 of 34 consonants+્ર come out as half form + full ra (ગ ઘ ઙ ચ છ ઞ ઠ ડ ઢ ણ થ ધ ન બ ભ મ ય ર લ વ ષ ળ). Only ગ is confirmed against the composer; the other 21 are expected but not verified. (5) Every one of the 16 names carries the text '(Shree-Lipi 7.0 / 4-5-6)', even on the 4/5/6-only faces, so the list cannot tell the user which family a font is. (6) The Font box lists all 140 Gujarati fonts (60 Ex, 9 x 7.0, 7 x 4/5/6, Terafont/ISFOC/etc., installed Bhasha Bharati faces) whatever layout is chosen. All 16 Shree 7/456 fonts are installed. howFontListIsBuilt:
There are two layers: the app code never filters the list, and the config puts the 7.0 and 4/5/6 families under one encoding.

APP CODE (main window):
(a) src/FontSoftware.App/ViewModels/MainViewModel.cs:534-542 (OnLanguageChanged) adds EVERY entry of SelectedLanguage.Fonts to the Fonts collection. It skips only missing Optional faces and never looks at the font layout. Lines 548-556 then append every installed family when 'Show all installed fonts' is on. MainWindow.xaml:449 binds the Font ComboBox straight to this collection.
(b) MainViewModel.cs:591-631 (OnFontLayoutChanged) only changes SelectedFont; it never clears or filters Fonts. So under Shree-Lipi 7.0 or 4.0/5.0/6.0, Gujarati shows all 140 fonts: 60 Ex, 9 SHREE-GUJ7, 7 SHREE-GUJ, Terafont, ISFOC and the rest.
(c) PickLayoutFont (MainViewModel.cs:640-649) returns null at :642-643 for any layout without 'encodings', which covers every Shree 7.0 and 4/5/6 row. Control falls through to :612-623, which selects the font whose id equals fl.FontId. Both Gujarati rows have fontId shree-guj-0750 = SHREE-GUJ-0750 (S07500F2.TTF, a 4/5/6 face), so picking 'Shree-Lipi 7.0' selects a 4/5/6 font. Every language except Kannada has the same pattern: the 7.0 row points at a SHREE-XXX- face, and Malayalam's 4/5/6 row points at a 7 face.
(d) FontLayout.Includes (src/FontSoftware.Core/Models/FontLayout.cs:57-60) matches by Encodings when present, else by id. It is used only by PickLayoutFont (:644), the combined-layout hint (:145) and :881, never to build the list. Even an encoding filter could not separate the families: every SHREE-GUJ and SHREE-GUJ7 entry has ConversionKey (FontAsset.cs:50) = 'shree-guj7', and AssetBundle.CreateConverterToLegacy (src/FontSoftware.Core/Config/AssetBundle.cs:101) picks the table by that key alone.
(e) UpdateLegacyFontHint (MainViewModel.cs:133-141) collects the installed families of ALL languages with that ConversionKey, which includes both families. LegacyFontName prefers SelectedFont.Family, which becomes the font the engine stamps into Word (:677-678, SetLegacyConverter). The '7.0' row therefore writes into SHREE-GUJ-0750.

APP CODE (converter page): ConverterViewModel.cs:572-588 gives both rows Key Legacy('shree-guj7'). As a result :638 refuses 7.0 -> 4/5/6 as 'Input and output layouts are the same', and RebuildFonts (:595-626) lists the layout font followed by every installed family (:620-624).

CONFIG GENERATION (why the data is shaped this way): tools/RegisterFonts/Program.cs:361-373 (--by-series) maps both GUJ7 and GUJ to 'shree-guj7'. It does the same for DEV7/DEV -> shree-dev456, BAN7/BAN/ASS7/ASS -> shree-ban7, KAN, MAL, ORI, PUN, TAM and TEL. Its cmap check at :434-437 cannot tell the families apart, because both map the same code points (217 for Gujarati). EncodingForLayout (:97-113) deliberately gives the '7.0' and '4.0' rows the same non-x encoding, with the comment 'Shree gives those two the same byte layout'. LegacyIdForLayout (:118-125) then takes the first font sorted by family name. 'SHREE-GUJ-0750' sorts before 'SHREE-GUJ7-0750' because '-' (0x2D) < '7' (0x37), so the 7.0 row lands on a 4/5/6 face in 11 of the 13 languages.

EVIDENCE that the families really differ: per-design outline comparison of 7.0 vs 4/5/6 files (scratchpad/shree7/fontlist-audit-7-vs-456-glyphcompare.txt and fontlist-audit-7-vs-456-glyphdiff.png).
- GUJ: 212/217 glyphs identical; 0xB6 and 0x91-0x94 differ.
- DEV: 0xB3, 0xB6, 0x91 and 0x92 differ, and the 456 faces have 45 extra codes.
- BAN/ASS: 0x25, 0x40, 0xA5, 0xA8, 0xFF, 0x8C, 0x96 and 0x97 differ.
- TAM: 0xBA, 0x9F and 0x9B differ.
- ORI, KAN and TEL: identical. PUN: identical except 0x3C.
So the claim that 7.0 and 4/5/6 share one byte layout is false for Gujarati, Devanagari, Bengali-script and Tamil.
whyTestsMissedIt:
Every check tests the table against itself or against the font's code-point list. None compares our bytes with what Shree's software writes, and none converts the multi-key syllable a typist actually produces.

1. Round trips cannot see this bug. tools/ConvTest/Program.cs:78-95, ConverterTests.ShreeRoundTripNoUnmapped (ConverterTests.cs:65-100, which has shree-guj7 rows only for શેરી and ધીરજ) and ConversionPipelineTests.LegacyToLegacyGoesThroughUnicode (:16-30) all assert Unicode -> legacy -> Unicode == input with no unmapped characters. ગ્ર -> C1 66 -> 'ગ્' + 'ર' = ગ્ર passes. Shree's 4E B0 also decodes to ગ્ર (checked with the shree-guj7-to-unicode table), so the test passes whichever bytes are written: a wrong but reversible table is indistinguishable from the right one. ConversionPipelineTests:29 even asserts only Assert.NotEqual(x, seven).

2. The word lists never contain a consonant + ્ર cluster in 7/456. ConvTest's discovered encodings use wordsByBlock[0x0A80] (:33): કમલ, નમસ્તે, વિદ્યા, ક્ષત્રિય, vowels and ક઼. Its explicit list (:10-21) covers only the X encodings. No test word contains ગ્ર, પ્ર, ક્ર or any other C+્ર in shree-guj7.

3. tools/FullTest presses keys one at a time. :153-158 collects k.Base, k.Shift and k.AltGr per key and :171-177 converts each string alone. On BPMK, u -> 'ગ' (4E) and 1 -> '્ર' (B0) each convert correctly; the whole-word conversion the engine actually does (TypingEngine.cs:813 ConvertText(_uniWord)) never runs on 'ગ્ર'. --runs adds layout.Sequences, but BPMK has no sequence for ગ્ર. A per-key Rosetta check would also pass: our table agrees with Shree's S8Guj764 answer on 93 of 99 BPMK keys (the rest are cp1252 spelling, ।, િ width and –), see scratchpad/shree7/bpmk-guj7.json.

4. FullTest's pass criterion is cmap membership (:189-207), a question of whether a code exists in the font, not whether it is the right glyph. SHREE-GUJ-0750 and SHREE-GUJ7-0750 map the same 217 code points, so C1 66 'exists' in both. The 0xB6 and 0x91-0x94 glyph differences between families are invisible, and so is the mixed table that uses 0x91 as ઙ્ક in one pair and as પ in another.

5. FullTest tests the layout's ONE font, plus every font with the same ConversionKey (:133-135). Because both families share 'shree-guj7', a 7.0 row pointing at a 4/5/6 face looks correct, and putting both families in one list is treated as intended.

6. The config checks only check that references resolve. tools/ConfigCheck/Program.cs:53-64 verifies that fontId exists, that the type matches and that a table exists. No test asserts that a 'Shree-Lipi 7.0' row's font is a *7 family or that the 4/5/6 row's is not, that two rows do not share one fontId, or that one id means the same family in every language. ConverterTests.EveryRegisteredLegacyFontHasBothDirections (:196-215) checks only that a table exists, and it skips the id 'shree-dev-0700'.

7. The typing-engine and selection tests are self-referential or never touch these layouts. TypingEngineTests (:394-402, :798-804, :613-623) assert _injector.Text == toLegacy.ConvertText(...), our own converter, so a wrong table is the expected value. They use shree-gujx or gopika, never shree-guj7. SelectionMemoryTests uses only gu-fl-shreelipi-ex. No test opens MainViewModel on a Shree 7.0 or 4/5/6 row and inspects Fonts or SelectedFont.

8. FontConverterTests (:9-62) test the greedy engine on a 4-pair toy table. They prove the longest match wins, which is exactly the behaviour that turns ગ્ર into 'ગ્' + 'ર' when the table lacks a 'ગ્ર' or C+'્ર' rule. 22 of 34 Gujarati consonants + ્ર come out as half form + full ra (0x66).

The ground truth exists but no test uses it. The S8Guj764 composer answers ગ = 4E and ્ર = B0 (BPMK capture). The S8GujG64 composer answered only 11 blank pairs, so there is no composer oracle for 4/5/6 yet. That oracle would have to come from Shree's Converter nxt (the GapFill path) or from rendering.
testGaps: Ground-truth byte test (the one that catches ગ્ર). Add a checked-in fixture captured from Shree's own composers: kbdcapture --rosetta --legacy 7 for every .GUJ keyboard, plus each keyboard's conjunct slots and two-key consonant+sign sequences (u,1 on BPMK). Assert CreateConverterToLegacy("shree-guj7").ConvertText(unicode) equals the exact bytes, for example ConvertText("ગ્ર") == "N°" (4E B0), not the round trip. Repeat for dev456/ban7/tam7/ori7/kan7/pun7/tel7/mal7.

Consonant x sign matrix: for every consonant and every sign key the composer answers (્ર, reph, matras, halant), compare our whole-cluster conversion with Shree's sequence answer, or render both byte strings in SHREE-GUJ7-0750 and compare ink. This flags the 22 consonants that come out as half form + 0x66.

Typing-engine test with a hard-coded expected value: BPMK layout, shree-guj7 converter, keys u then 1, assert _injector.Text == "N°". Do not compare against our own toLegacy.ConvertText, which makes the current TypingEngineTests self-fulfilling.

Family-separation config test: for each language, a 'Shree-Lipi 7.0' row's font family must match ^SHREE-[A-Z]{3}7-|^Shree-[A-Za-z]{3}7- (files *890/*892/*896/W*7*), and a '4.0/5.0/6.0' row's must match ^SHREE-[A-Z]{3}-\d (*0F0/*0F2/*0F6). The two rows must not share a fontId. Today this fails in 11 languages (Malayalam's 4/5/6 row is a 7 face).

Encoding-separation test: no single encoding id may contain both SHREE-XXX7 and SHREE-XXX fonts unless a glyph comparison proves the faces identical. For GUJ, DEV, BAN/ASS and TAM they are not identical: 5, 4, 8 and 3 differing bytes respectively.

Table-consistency test: within one table, a legacy byte must decode to one base glyph. shree-guj7 maps 0x91 to ઙ્ક alone and to પ inside '‘p¡'; the same holds for 0x92 and 0x93. Also render each table's single-byte pairs in a representative font of EACH family it claims and compare with the Unicode text (GlyphJoin-style).

MainViewModel font-list test: select gu-fl-shree-lipi-7-0 and assert that Fonts (the Font box) contains only SHREE-GUJ7/Shree-Guj7 faces, that SelectedFont is one of them, and that LegacyFontName is a 7 face. Then do the same for 4.0/5.0/6.0 with SHREE-GUJ faces. Today Fonts holds all 140 Gujarati fonts and SelectedFont is SHREE-GUJ-0750 for both rows.

Converter-page test: Shree-Lipi 7.0 -> Shree-Lipi 4.0/5.0/6.0 must be convertible, or at least not reported as 'Input and output layouts are the same' (ConverterViewModel.cs:638). RebuildFonts should list only the layout's family before the 'all installed' tail.

ID-uniqueness test: a font id must name the same family in every language. 'shree-dev-0700' is SHREE-DEVX-0700 in Hindi but SHREE-DEV-0700 in Marathi and Sanskrit, and ConverterTests.cs:208 skips it. Also check that no family name is carried by two different installed files used as one entry (SHREE-ORI7-0603 = S0603892 + WORI7001, which differ in 7 glyphs).
Label test: font names must not say '(Shree-Lipi 7.0 / 4-5-6)'. A name should state the one family the face belongs to: 16 Gujarati, 10 Odia and 12 Tamil entries carry the combined label today.

Missing-family test: a layout row whose family has no installed font, for example Malayalam 4.0/5.0/6.0 with no SHREE-MAL face, must show 'not installed' instead of quietly using another family's font.
Ex-row guard (already partly done in commit 58d8d3e): keep a test that the ShreeLipi-Ex row's font is a *X family and the 7.0/4-5-6 rows' fonts are never *X.
